react_result.final_narrative_text: Metabolomics profiling of 13 differentially abundant metabolites reveals robust perturbation of sulfur amino acid metabolism and connected one-carbon folate pathways across three independent analytical paradigms. RaMP multi-database ORA identifies KEGG:map00260 "Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism" as the dominant signal (FDR=3.75e-19, 8/57 metabolites hit), while KEGG:map00270 "Methionine Metabolism" ranks 4th (FDR=1.19e-13, 6/51 metabolites hit). MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific PSEA confirms KEGG:hsa00670 "One carbon pool by folate" as its top pathway (p=3.36e-07, 5/26 metabolites hit), directly linking the methionine cycle to folate-dependent one-carbon transfer. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently recovers both the methionine/cysteine module and the glycine/serine/threonine module as top-3 network hits (p=0.016 each), and additionally implicates MUMM:arachidonic_acid_metabolism (p=0.016) via 15-HETE and 8(S)-HPETE accumulation. The driver metabolites—homocysteine (C00155), S-adenosylmethionine (C00019), L-methionine (C00073), choline (C00114), L-threonine (C00188), cysteic acid (C00506), and 15-HETE (C04742)—form a coherent biological cluster centered on methionine salvage, transsulfuration, and phospholipid/mediator metabolism. Disruption of this hub suggests impaired methylation capacity and perturbed lipid mediator production in the treatment condition.
